mission.title: Induction
mission.description: Invite the intruder on a tour of what only the Merovingian's organization can offer.

npc.say: Go ahead. I'll pass the time by picking this one's brain.
Yes...some of us did survive. His knowledge is curious--both its extent, and its gaps.
Get him out of here... Hurry it up!
What, there's more? Well, let's have it.
I told him what he'd have wanted to hear about my work. Isn't that what you wanted?
No. I've got some things to take care of.

phase.briefing:
Cerulean turned out to be quite adept at locating the intruder, operative, once she received a little help from our own resources. A strange fellow... He's been haunting the Heart o' the City Hotel, for instance, for no apparent reason. But there must be something to what he's doing, or else the Machines wouldn't be in such a tizzy over it. Do you know, he actually fought them off by using their own programs against them! Rather droll, actually...
Yes, the fact is that we feel it's time to make this man's acquaintance. I wouldn't send you in to make the first impression, except that he has a knack for deleting programs, which has proven awfully expensive for us so far. You're not going to impress him with your own dubious merits, of course; you're going to invite him on a tour of the city, the likes of which only our organization can provide. If that old roach hotel fascinates him, this should blow his wires off.

enter.say:
Are you ready for this? This guy's putting out power readings like...well, like I've never seen before. Would probably be bad for your future children, if your RSI could actually sustain permanent damage...
Anyway, good luck.

talk.say:
A Frenchman? I've known a few of those... A tour of the city, you say? Huh.
All right. Why not? Impress me.

done.say: Okay. It sounds like Flood's going to have courier programs direct the guy. And Flood wants to talk to you, so head outside.

near.say: Power readings are climbing. You must be getting close.
Holy-- I've got to dampen down my scan settings. The feedback from him and that...thing nearly locked up my monitoring program.

phase.briefing: It isn't as easy as it should be to come up with people to introduce him to who can display impressive credentials, without also suffering from significant character flaws, but I've come up with a few. First of all, it seems only fitting that we should parade Cerulean before him. He might be interested in her information tracking abilities; she found him, after all.

enter.say: Okay, just break the ice for those two. Presumably, Flood's already coached Cerulean on what to say this guy...

talk.say: Yes. Pleased to meet you. My name is Cerulean; I assist the Merovingian with data tracking tasks from time to time. I was instrumental in locating you, for instance. The vast majority of the Matrix's information is transparent to us, and we are uniquely situated to pursue it, when we wish.

An incorporeal program? Yes, I'm sure she can access quite a few interesting pieces of information.
I didn't expect to find this sort of mutation here. Must be pretty irritating for the Machines.
Got anything else to show me?

done.say: Sounds like we've got him interested. Let's see what else Flood wants us to show him.

phase.briefing: Cerulean charmed him, did she? That was easier than I thought it would be. Very well, if he found her interesting, he ought to be thrilled meeting a vampire and a werewolf.

enter.say: I hope someone's got Ookami on a short leash there.

talk.say: --and I believe you'll find our intelligence network second to none. We are much more...flexible than the Machines in the ways in which we can observe, assist, influence, or kill...as the case requires. You will not find us hampered by illusions of morality, or subservience to ephemeral ideals. Our means are effective, and our ends practical.

I get it, but I won't prance like the pony. This man is dangerous. Stupid to try to keep him here.
Hrah! Are we done? Only an idiot stands next to a bomb longer than he has to.

done.say: Hm... I don't know if I've ever heard Ookami sound that worried before.

talk.say: Very cold, for a blood-sucker. How amusing that some of these survived. I see the Machines aren't nearly as in-control as they like to appear. Should I be concerned for this world's stability? Haha!

done.say: I'm not sure I like it when this guy laughs. And what he said about Malphas... He's talking about that earlier version of the Matrix...

phase.briefing:
Certainly, he could have killed them if he'd wanted to. There is a reason why we take the trouble to make frequent backups of important personnel, you know. Oh, it would have been a little inconvenient and expensive if he had killed them, but I knew he wouldn't. I can read people, you know; don't worry, nobody's interested in you...
The last personality on our little tour actually called me before I had to take the trouble to look her up. If only everyone I worked with was so considerate...

enter.say: Huh. After the MacHenry pod thing, I had the impression Hypatia was looking to get out from under the Merv's thumb for a while. Guess I'm no Flood.

talk.say: --of the Archivist Society. We have compiled an incomparable library of information from previous versions of the Matrix. Access is highly restricted, of course, but for a researcher such as yourself, allowances would be made. We are very interested in the exchange of historical data. Anything you might wish to know is open to negotiation.

done.say: Whoa, hold on. Is she kissing up to him for the Merv, or for herself?

talk.say:
Huh. Maybe you people know more than I'd thought, but I'm not much into ancient history right now.
Anyway... The Merovingian, was it? I'll remember that.

done.say: I've got a feeling that guy isn't really into books.

mission.finish:
What?! If that four-eyed geek has queered this deal--
Why didn't you shut her up, {player}? What did I have you there for, anyway?
If she thinks she's going to make some sort of private arrangement with him, she's in for a rude awakening. This is our pigeon--make no mistake about that.
